title: ET Module 6 The Diffusion of Emerging Technologies FA25
published: FA25 filename; exact release date not stated
observed: Course theory, not a technology survey
claim: Diffusion stages, adopter categories, five factors and communication actors; slides 27/52/54 present 16% and messaging heuristics.
limits: Heuristics require a matching innovation/social system and evidence. Old end-of-deck assignments do not replace current Assignment 5 memo.

title: The state of AI in 2026 On the road to ROI
observed: Online survey 2026-05-04 to 2026-06-08; 1,719 respondents in 97 nations; results weighted by national GDP
claim: Respondents in the report-defined large-revenue group reporting agent scaling in one or more functions increased from 27% in the previous survey to 40%; smaller-organization respondents report 22%, essentially unchanged. Agent scaling varies by function and industry.
limits: Respondent self-reports, not a census of unique firms or the eventual adopter population. Scope is agent scaling in any function, not chart-to-source reconciliation or comparable US mid-sized financial firms. Differing survey samples/definitions cannot prove individual firms advanced or a Rogers quantile. No firm revenue supplied in the case.
locator: Agent-use discussion/Exhibit 2 and About the research

title: Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users
observed: BTOS data 2025-12-14 through 2026-05-03; current-use question concerns previous two weeks
claim: At the period ending 2026-05-03, Finance and Insurance reports 33.9% using AI in any business function, compared with 19.8% nationally. The core AI wording broadened in November 2025.
limits: Broad AI, not agentic AI, chart checking, or an installed agent base. Older snapshot; not October 2026 prevalence. Expected next-six-month use is intention, not observed implementation. Do not combine with S1 percentages or compare across wording breaks as an unqualified growth rate.
locator: AI Trends Across Sectors and question-wording explanation

title: Building effective agents
observed: Vendor engineering experience; historical design guidance
claim: Distinguishes model-directed tools from predefined workflows and discusses cost, complexity and compounding-error tradeoffs.
limits: Mechanism/context evidence only. Not a diffusion-rate estimate, independent local efficacy trial or October 2026 reliability score; live page notes tooling changes.

title: Model Context Protocol specification 2025-11-25
claim: Defines a common connection architecture for model applications, tools and context, with security/consent considerations.
limits: Protocol existence may reduce an integration barrier in principle; it neither measures adoption share nor proves universal interoperability, compliance or chart-review effectiveness. Use as an ecosystem mechanism, not diffusion proof.
